The equation $x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 6$ represents an ellipse. The normal line at the point $(\sqrt{2}, 1)$ on the ellipse intersects the $x$-axis at the point $P$. What are the coordinates of $P$?
corrected_content.worked_solution: Implicit differentiation gives the tangent slope $-x/(4y)=-1/(2\sqrt2)$ at $(\sqrt2,1)$. The normal slope is its negative reciprocal, $2\sqrt2$. Thus the normal is $y-1=2\sqrt2(x-\sqrt2)$. Setting $y=0$ yields $$x=\sqrt2-\frac1{2\sqrt2}=\frac3{2\sqrt2}.$$ Therefore $P=(\tfrac3{2\sqrt2},0)$.
